design:
D1. Routing is decided once at send time from bindings, independent of how the entry is later delivered or displayed, and is specified apart from delivery so each rule set stays small enough to check against its code.

D2. Resolution order: a named conversation, the forward binding on the sender's line of work (the sender's identity when there is no sending conversation), the reverse binding, then a new bound conversation. Never recency.
lifecycle: Split out of agent-conversation-workspace in the 2026-10-08 spec overhaul.
problem: Senders do not hold recipient conversation ids. If routing chose by recency, a correspondent's messages would scatter across whatever conversation the recipient touched last, and a reply would not reach the thread it answers.

requirements.rationale: Senders do not hold recipient conversation ids, so this rule governs almost all peer traffic; matching the line rather than one id keeps a correspondent on the same thread across a cutover.
requirements.statement: A peer message that names no recipient conversation SHALL be delivered to the recipient conversation bound to the sending conversation's line of work (the conversation plus every predecessor and successor linked by checkpoint cutover), creating that binding, with `origin: peer`, on first use; delivery MUST NOT be selected by the recipient's recency.

requirements.rationale: One durable thread per source and recipient leaves no path on which recency routing survives.
requirements.statement: A message from a source that has no conversation (the Hub or the scheduler) SHALL be delivered to a recipient conversation bound to that source's identity.

requirements.rationale: A sender that named an archived thread made a correctable error; a thread the operator archived is not the sender's doing.
requirements.statement: Delivery to an archived recipient conversation SHALL be refused, with the message content returned, when the sender named it, and SHALL continue into a newly bound successor conversation when the binding resolved it.

requirements.rationale: Resolution order is named conversation, forward binding, reverse binding, then creation, so every delivery the forward binding resolves is unchanged and a reply finds the thread it answers.
requirements.statement: When a peer message names no recipient conversation and no forward binding resolves, delivery SHALL follow the sending conversation's own binding in reverse: if it is bound to a conversation owned by the recipient, the message SHALL be delivered into the newest open conversation of that conversation's line of work rather than into a new conversation.

requirements.rationale: An agent needs a way to separate a genuinely new line of work outside a checkpoint cutover; honouring either half of a contradictory request would discard the caller's intent.
requirements.statement: The outbound message surface (`POST /messages`, MCP `send_message`) SHALL accept `start_new_thread`, defaulting to false, which creates a recipient conversation bound to the sending conversation without consulting either binding, so later messages on that line reach it; combining it with a named `conversation_id` SHALL be refused with the content returned.

in_scope: The forward binding from the sending conversation's line of work, across checkpoint cutovers
The reverse binding that carries a reply into the thread it answers
Traffic from sources with no conversation (the Hub, the scheduler)
Archived recipient threads, by whether the sender named it or a binding resolved it
non_goals: Delivering the queued entry once routed, and the hop budget: inbound-queue-delivery
Archiving conversations and their origin marking: conversation-lifecycle
Rendering peer messages in the transcript: agent-conversation-workspace
The checkpoint cutover that links a line of work: agent-conversation-handoff

summary: Which conversation an agent-to-agent message lands in. A message that names no conversation follows the forward binding from the sending conversation's line of work, falls back to the reverse binding so a reply continues the thread it answers, binds to the sender's identity when the source has no conversation, is refused or redirected at an archived thread depending on who chose it, and can deliberately start a new thread.
title: Peer message routing
